title: Bar Chavu
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a scribe who wrote tefillin and mezuzot in Abaye’s time. Megillah 18b says that Abaye permitted Bar Chavu’s household to write tefillin and mezuzot without a written exemplar. In Bava Metzia 29b Abaye says that tefillin are readily available in Bar Chavu’s household. Hyman cites Berakhot 53b for Abaye’s blessing over the light at the close of Shabbat. He notes that the Gemara reads Bar Avuha and reports the reading Bar Chavu from Dikdukei Soferim.
Eruvin 15a mentions the barka, a standing post, at Bar Chavu’s house, over which Abaye and Rava disputed all their days.
And we find Ada bar Chavu in Chullin 75b, in the time of Rav Ashi, and Rav Yosef bar Chavu in Yoma 87a.

notes.text: The source prints אביו, “his father,” although the examples are all in Abaye’s time; this is not silently corrected. The malformed רולי שנייהו is read through the checked כולי שנייהו, “all their days.” Barka denotes the post at issue in the boundary discussion.

No new primary scalar was returned. Supplied אביו means his father; Abaye is a plausible contextual correction but other entries do not prove a recurring vav/yod error here. Hyman’s opening occupation/time assertion is attributed without silently replacing father with Abaye. The earlier Eruvin comparison supports all their days beside malformed רולי שנייהו and the boundary-post sense of barka; it is not newly inspected. BarAvuha/Chavu variants are Hyman’s report, not fresh DikdukeiSoferim collation. Ada and Yosef patronymics are not assumed one family; full Rav Ashi and Rav Yosef remain.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. I, p. 286) reads “in Abaye’s time” (בזמן אביי) and “all their days” (כולי שנייהו). The supplied Wikisource transcription has אביו (“his father”) and רולי. The print also reads כותב (“who wrote”) where the transcription has כותר. Megillah 18b and Bava Metzia 29b explicitly name Abaye and Bar Chavu’s household. Eruvin 15a confirms the household and “all their days.” The consulted Berakhot 53b instead reads Bar Avuha, and the Dikdukei Soferim variant is reported by Hyman. Chullin 75b names Ada before Rav Ashi, while Yoma 87a names Rav Yosef before Rabbi Abbahu. Those two patronymics do not establish a family relationship.
